advisory.summary: Same synthetic SSRF sink as the reachable/unreachable legs, in a build where one source file the directory walk lists cannot be read. Tool-failure shape: the analysis degrades to Partial(tool_failure) rather than silently rendering an incomplete index as complete. Empirically confirmed reachable via a committed DANGLING SYMLINK named *.py whose target does not exist -- see finding F-B3 / the C4 table.

acquisition.notes: First-party Python repro. src/app.py is a real, readable module (open_conn present and reachable). src/vendored_shim.py is a COMMITTED DANGLING SYMLINK (git mode 120000, target does_not_exist_sidecar.py) whose *.py name is listed by the scanner's directory walk but whose os.ReadFile follows the link and fails -> readFailed -> Partial(tool_failure) (index.go:62-64,80-82; callgraph.go:100-104,198-200). Empirically verified portable: git stores the symlink as mode 120000 and a fresh checkout re-creates it dangling (core.symlinks default true). This is NOT the missing/empty-build-dir case (that is a hard error, index.go:47-59). No target code is executed.

expected_verdict.label: undetermined
expected_verdict.rationale: One source file listed by the directory walk cannot be read (a committed dangling symlink), so the index and call graph degrade to Partial(tool_failure) while still emitting the symbols from the readable file. The result never renders the unknown as a complete, successful index. Verdict correctness is out of scope for PLAN-070; C4 asserts the tool_failure partiality arm, not an empty successful result.
